doc.title: John Beal interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 18, 2024

title: Woody Herman band, 1955
summary: Beal joined Woody Herman at 19 in 1955 for about a year of one-nighters with Nat Pierce and Richie Kamuca; travel was by car and a broken-down bus, once a school bus to Newport.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Lost in translation. So you were a young man with, when you went with Woody Herman.
’55 I got the gig, yeah. I was there for about a year and then they broke the band up.
Were you sorry the band broke up? Were you enjoying it?
Oh yeah. Yeah. It was great. Yeah I really enjoyed it. Nat Pierce was there, Richie Kamuka, you know, it was a lot of fun. Mostly one-nighters for a year. I think I was 19 when I got in that band.
That’s good. That’s a young man’s game doing that.
Yeah. And I still play on the same instrument. I have played on different instruments but I’ve been playing that bass for 70 years. And it’s the best it’s ever sounded right now.
How did the band get around at that time? Did you have a luxurious bus?

Well no, it was cars and we got paid an extra $25 for driving. And then there was a couple of wrecks you know and then they got a bus. And it was a kind of broken down bus. To go in reverse the driver had to go out and stick a broom handle into the transmission. I remember we played at Newport Jazz Festival once and the bus had broken down so they had to get a school bus, and we showed up at Newport in a school bus.
“Ladies and Gentlemen, The Woody Herman Orchestra here they come in the yellow bus.”
Yeah. But it was a swinging band you know, it was a lot of fun.
